findings.issue: The ar17 comment says the redo is refused because the commit the read builds is checked against what git status lists in the tree. The refusal ar17 actually sees comes from tree_undescribed (the forced file is staged in the index as neither its base nor the work holds it), because _unheld counts an ignored file the scratch index lacks as held. The executor's own notes say so, and the mutation log agrees: the row 'carry commit trusted, never checked against the files' turns ar17b and ar17c red but not ar17. So ar17 would stay green with carry_commit's status-versus-scratch check deleted, and its title and comment name the wrong layer.
findings.resolution: Reword the ar17 comment and title to say the staged-state question refuses a forced file the read misses, and leave the status-versus-scratch check to ar17b and ar17c. Or point ar17 at a path the read misses that is not ignored, so it reaches carry_commit's check.

intent.note: Judged against the clauses of the task description. (1) 'a tree holding ANY gitlink entry (in its index, its HEAD or the carry) or any nested .git refuses the recut, whatever git's ignore settings say. Every status and diff the check runs uses --ignore-submodules=none': tree_undescribed (drive-phase.py:5018-5080) reads mode 160000 off ls-files -s, ls-tree HEAD and ls-tree <work commit>, and walks the disk for a .git below the top with _nested_repositories. recut_tree calls it before carry_beside_work, keep_redo_work and drop_tree. tree_changed, _changed_between, _unheld, carry_commit's cached diff, tree_work's patch diff and the diff-index calls all pass --ignore-submodules=none. (2) over-fire: _unheld now passes --exclude-standard, and ar19 covers it. (3) staged-only state: the index is treated as part of the work and the recut refuses by name. A path staged against HEAD that the work commit also does not hold is refused (diff-index --cached against HEAD and against the work, intersected, record paths left out). That covers rm --cached of an unignored file (ar20) and the staged edit with the file put back (ar20b). A staged edit the file still shows is carried (ar20c). Nothing is dropped silently. (4) the lows: skip-worktree copied only for a file absent from disk (ar21), assume-unchanged files read from disk (ar17c), redo_left's fallback no longer prescribes an apply over a tree that may hold the work, via redo_held and ar6d, ar6e and ar6f, path bytes kept through _git_path (ar22), and _seed_from_index's docstring now says what it copies. The claim describes the diff: each function, case id and doc paragraph it names exists, and work['links'], _links_added and _links_touched are gone with no other reader (git grep found none outside drive-phase.py and its suite). Dependants: no file outside drive-phase.py, its suite, _deps.py and the guide names the changed functions, so the executor's 'still correct' answers hold. The two rows added to GIT_PATH_BASE_EXEMPT sit in _deps.py. The claim's scope notes are accurate: tree_holds_only_integrated (the retire path) is left and the filed return says so; the orchestrator says a follow-up task takes it up. The guide's case lists omit ar17c and ar18f, which is cosmetic. No F/P/BUG ids appear in the added code lines.
